images.filename: Living History Exhibits at Lincoln Boyhood National Memorial, Indiana (1206e586-75d0-4131-94a0-cae6dd50033a).jpg
images.caption:
Interpretive staff outside cabin
Lincoln Boyhood National Memorial preserves the site of the farm where Abraham Lincoln spent 14 formative years of his life, from the ages of 7 to 21. He and his family moved to Indiana in 1816 and stayed until 1830 when they moved on to Illinois. The time he spent here helped shape the man that went on to lead the country. This site is our most direct tie with that time of his life.
Keywords: libo; living history; National memorials; Interpretive programs; Presidents; Homes; Lincoln; Abraham; 1809-1865

images.filename: Grave of Nancy Hanks Lincoln, mother of Abraham Lincoln. The grave is located in the Pioneer Cemetery at Lincoln Boyhood (e57a66fb-7090-411c-a78e-c1002e625ac2).jpg
images.caption:
White marble grave marker, rectangular at the bottom, comes to a point at the top. Text: Nancy Hanks Lincoln mother of President Lincoln, died Oct 5 AD 1818 Aged 25 years, erected by friend of her martyred son 1879. Green grass all around, trees and iron fence in background.  Pennies on the ground in front of the grave.
The white marble headstone marks the grave of Abraham Lincoln's mother, Nancy Hanks Lincoln.  Nancy died on October 5, 1818.  She was 36 years old.
Keywords: Abraham Lincoln; cemetery
